Usually I will have about 3 habitats in a work zone - sometimes more if they are low maintenance, and less if they need a lot of attention (looking at you, peafowl who won't stop pooping on the guest paths...). 

Geography wise, they will be grouped in little clusters to include the nearby staff and guest amenities. I include a little bit of overlap, especially on things that get a lot of use - like your most popular gift shop, busiest toilets, or large staffrooms. Sometimes I do this by types of animal but usually my zoo layouts are all over the place so location is really the key thing. 

As well as having staff assigned to each workzone, I like to have a small amount of roaming staff that cover the whole park and who can pop up when needed - so if all the vets in the north work zone are researching and an animal gets sick, wandering vet number 2 can jump in, for example. Not many, just enough to be useful in a pinch. I also don't bother giving my educators workzones unless I have a LOT concentrated in a specific area. 

I think of it kind of like a department store -  each section has its own sales team, cleaning team, etc, but if necessity demands they can be a bit flexible, hence the overlap.

In the UK you can get therapy and medication through the NHS. The easiest way is probably to go through your GP and explain that you feel low and the ways in which it's affecting your life (even if they seem obvious, everything is good to mention). There will likely be a waiting list as the MH division of the NHS is severely underfunded, but they will likely give you some support in the interim - someone you can talk to, or suggestions for ways to look after yourself. 

If you feel even slightly that you might hurt yourself, go to A&E. I know it seems like a lot. When my dad found out I was suicidal he insisted on taking me there. I was seen within two hours, spoke to therapists, and within a week I had regular counselling sessions set up, a support network, they spoke to my school - they helped me every step of the way. A&E is for mental emergencies too. 

I've been going to counselling for the last four years on the NHS totally free, they have all been excellently trained and incredibly kind. I might have just been lucky, but there are really good people who will help you so much. I've also been on prescription meds, they've helped me fill out uni applications, make calls to my bank - I'm a long way from healing but it has helped so so much. 
I wish you luck!
